title: Reservation service and allocation
idea: The core design is one ReservationService that finds the free tables for a slot and asks an injected TableAllocationStrategy which one the party gets.

analogy.text: A head waiter with a seating chart. The waiter checks which tables are free at seven, then follows the house rule for who sits where.
analogy.breaks: Changing the house rule here means passing a new object, not retraining.

points: ReservationService is a facade: callers see `book`, not tables or schedules.
`TableAllocationStrategy` is the strategy pattern; best fit is one rule.
`ReservationRepository` hides storage: a map now, PostgreSQL on page 6.
The `Clock` and id supplier are injected, so every run prints the same.

steps.caption: A customer asks for a table for four at 19:00.
The service checks the start against the `Clock`, then builds a 90-minute TimeSlot.
For each table it reads that table's reservations and keeps tables with no overlap.
The free list goes to the strategy. Best fit picks the smallest table that seats four.
T3 is chosen. The service saves a Reservation through the repository.
The Reservation returns to the caller. The service never knew the allocation rule.
When no free table fits, the strategy returns empty and the service refuses with NO_TABLE.

code.title: Service and interfaces
code.caption: The core flow. Every collaborator is passed into the constructor. Reservation is trimmed to a record; page 4 adds status rules.

walk.text: A fixed `Clock` at noon and four tables: one for two, two for four, one for six.
Wire the service with best fit, an in-memory repository and a counter for ids.
Six requests: five at 19:00 and a couple at 20:30, right after the first seating.
A start before the clock's noon is refused.
Best fit: the smallest capacity that seats the party, ties broken by id.
Keep only tables whose reservations do not overlap the new slot.
Ask the strategy, refuse with NO_TABLE when empty, else save and return.

code.title: A new rule, no edits
code.caption: A decorator strategy keeps the six-seat table for bigger parties. The service and best fit are unchanged.

walk.text: Wrap best fit: tables of six or more only go to parties of four or more.
Two free lists: an earlier time with T3 and T4, a late time with T4 only.
Ask both strategies for a couple and for a party of five.
Small parties see a filtered list; big parties pass straight through to the inner rule.

pitfalls: Do not put allocation rules inside `book`; each new rule would edit the service.
Never call `Instant.now()` inside the service; inject a `Clock` so tests control time.
Check overlap per table, not per restaurant; other tables stay bookable.

quiz.q: Which line does CoreReservation print for the fourth request?
quiz.why: T2 and T3 already hold overlapping 19:00 reservations. The only free table that seats four is T4, so best fit returns it.

takeaway: One service runs the flow; strategies decide which table, swapped without edits.

starters: Is best fit always the right allocation rule?
How is a decorator strategy different from a subclass?
Where would table combining fit in this design?
